products.title: Steamin' Sumatra Single Serve Pour Over
products.body_html:
Roast: Dark
Notes: Tobacco, herbal, clean earthy, woody, spicy
Region: Takengon highlands, Aceh, Sumatra
Process: Giling Basah (wet-hulled), sun-dried
Species: 100% Arabica
Certifications: Fair Trade Organic

Like the volcanoes of Sumatra, this coffee is steeped with geothermal energy that has traveled up from the center of the earth. The richness of the lower octave volcanic soil emanates from the beans offering it earthy, rich, and spicy flavor notes. Like the Miles Davis Quintet album of the same name, Steamin' is uniquely indelible with modal tones and depth that will make it an instant favorite at first sip.

products.title: "Ear Candy" Natural Processed Ethiopia - Single Serve Pourover
products.body_html:
Enjoy our Ethiopia Ear Candy in a handy on-the-go package with our single serve pourover option. The exterior pouches that hold the single serve pour over filters are biodegradable to reduce our carbon footprint but also nitro-flushed and ultrasonically sealed to ensure freshness and flavor. Simple tear the filter, fasten the arms of the filter to your mug or cup and pour 8oz of hot water through the filter. You can also use these for cold brew!

This single-serve is produced as a collaboration project with our friends at Pour Ta in Lamarie, WY.

products.title: Colombia Love Supremo - Single Origin
products.body_html:
Listen to our Colombia "Love Supremo" Spotify Playlist 


SUPREMO GRADE, Medium Roast

Notes: Cherry, Chocolate, Nutty
Region: Nariño
Altitude: 1,600 - 2,200 masl
Process: Washed
Species: 100% Arabica

A nod to both the peak grade of Colombian coffee (Supremo) and what is arguably the peak of John Coltrane's repertoire (A Love Supreme), "Love Supremo" is bright enough for breakfast and rich enough for dinner. Grown in Southwest Colombia, in the Nariño region along the Pacific coast, this roast has a creamy silkiness, bright acidity, and complex cocoa and cherry flavors with a sweet long finish. Like 'Trane's four-part masterpiece, this roast is resonant, profound and transcendent.

products.title: Frequency: The Fermentation Tasting Project
products.body_html:
FREQUENCY

The Fermentation Tasting Project — Three Keys Coffee × James Hoffmann

PRE-ORDER: Roasting Sept 12-15; Shipping Sept 16-18.

One coffee. Four fermentation paths. Same farm, same variety, same 48-hour window — only the fermentation itself changes. The result: Acoustic, Live, Treble, Bass — four expressions of a single Guatemalan lot.

🎧 Global live tasting with James Hoffmann — Saturday, October 3, 2026, ~9:00 AM Central

ACOUSTIC

Mechanically Demucilaged · WASHED

The coffee, stripped back. Washed process. This is the reference point for everything else. That makes Acoustic our control: the closest look at the coffee before fermentation begins shaping its flavor.

Think of it as an acoustic performance: no added effects, just the source material.

LIVE

Wild Fermentation · 48 Hours

Live undergoes a 48-hour fermentation driven by the naturally occurring microorganisms already present in the coffee's environment.
There is no selected bacteria or yeast added to direct the process. Instead, the local microbial community does what it has traditionally done in coffee processing: consumes sugars in the mucilage and produces compounds that can influence what we eventually experience in the cup.

That's why we call it Live: the same source material, shaped by the energy and unpredictability of a live performance.

TREBLE

Lactobacillus Inoculated · 48 Hours

The coffee is intentionally inoculated with Lactobacillus, bacteria known for producing organic acids during fermentation. Those acids can influence how we perceive brightness, acidity and complexity in the finished coffee, bringing certain characteristics forward with greater definition and lift.


We call it Treble for what happens at the high end: brightness turned up.

BASS

Saccharomyces Yeast Inoculated · 48 Hours

Inoculated with selected yeast for fuller body and layered complexity. The coffee is fermented for 48 hours with selected Saccharomyces yeast. During fermentation, the yeast produces compounds and flavor precursors that can influence the coffee's eventual sensory profile, particularly its body and complexity.

We call it Bass for the weight, depth, and texture. 

HOW TO TASTE

  1. Acoustic — your reference point, washed process
  2. Live — what changes when fermentation begins
  3. Treble — brightness, acidity, complexity
  4. Bass — body, depth, texture

Then go back — Acoustic beside Treble, Live beside Bass. The point isn't which is "best." It's discovering what fermentation actually tastes like.

Variety ~85% Caturra, ~15% H1, small amount Bourbon
Farm Finca San Miguel Urias — Hector & Lilian Leal, Rueda Farms
Location Antigua Valley, Guatemala
Altitude 1460–1540 masl
Included 4 × 100g bags (400g total) — one of each
